Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's global/top-level scope only sets variables (pkgbase, pkgname, arch, url, license, etc.) and defines no dangerous functions. The `source` array contains a GitHub archive URL (https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/archive/refs/tags/oxlint_v${pkgver}.tar.gz) and a local install script (oxlint.install). Both are standard AUR sources; the URL fetches the upstream release tarball, and the install script is a maintainer-provided file already present in the AUR repo. The `sha256sums` are provided (not SKIP), so the downloaded archive will be verified during extraction. There is no `pkgver()` function, and no top‑level code, `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or other network‑fetching commands that would execute during the sourcing step. The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are excluded by `--nobuild --noprepare`. Consequently, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` merely downloads and extracts the declared sources and parses the PKGBUILD without executing any malicious payload.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR source fetch, no malicious code
</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .gitignore:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.gitignore` file for an AUR package. It contains three entries: `*.tar.*` (ignoring tar archive files), `pkg` (the makepkg build output directory), and `src` (the source extraction directory). These are conventional `.gitignore` patterns used across virtually all Arch Linux package repositories to prevent build artifacts from being committed. There is no executable code, no network operations, no obfuscation, and no file system manipulation — nothing that could pose a security risk.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard .gitignore with no security concerns.</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/4] Reviewing .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD, oxlint.install...
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD packages the legitimate `oxc` project (oxlint and oxfmt) from its official upstream repository at `https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc`. The source is downloaded from the project's own GitHub releases via a tarball URL with a pinned tag, and both source files have proper SHA256 checksums.

The build process uses standard tooling: `cargo build --frozen` for the Rust oxlint binary (with `--frozen` ensuring the Cargo.lock is respected), and `pnpm` for the JavaScript oxfmt build. The `package_oxfmt()` function wisely uses `pnpm install --offline --prod --ignore-scripts` when installing production-only node_modules for the final package, which prevents arbitrary postinstall scripts from running at build time.

No suspicious operations are present: no `curl|bash` patterns, no base64-decoded payloads, no eval, no data exfiltration, no unexpected network requests, and no `git pull`/`git fetch` operations that could bypass the pinned source. The install procedures are conventional — copying compiled binaries, licenses, and node_modules into `$pkgdir`, plus creating a simple node.js wrapper script for the oxfmt CLI. The `rm -rf node_modules` cleanup operations are standard hygiene to keep dev-only dependencies out of the package.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR PKGBUILD for oxc project, no malicious behavior detected.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
